topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy launches DOE-backed "StabilityMax" AI data center fuel-cell testbed in Danbury, CT.
topSignals.text: FuelCell Energy will host a three-year collaborative project, led by the US Department of Energy's National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) with Argonne National Laboratory participating, to build data-center load-profile models and simulations (NLR) and techno-economic/lifecycle analyses (Argonne), alongside a physical fuel-cell test facility FuelCell Energy will develop at its Connecticut manufacturing site. No funding amount or MW capacity was disclosed, and the announcement does not specify whether the testbed uses FuelCell Energy's carbonate (SureSource) or solid-oxide (Advanced Technologies) product line — so this cannot yet be confirmed as SOFC-specific. The project builds on FuelCell Energy's existing 2026 collaboration with Siemens on a "layered architecture" power approach. Manila Times/GlobeNewswire

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21, 2026 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 51 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27, 2026 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 76 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by PTX/ammonia/SAF/blue-hydrogen news, out of SOFC/SOEC scope.
FuelCell Energy (Tier 2): Genuinely new item today — the DOE-backed "StabilityMax" data-center fuel-cell testbed announced Nov 10 (see Top Signals); fuel-cell chemistry not confirmed as SOFC.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Ceres Power, Mitsubishi Power — new cycle, round 1): no new item for either; Mitsubishi Power's circulating headline today ("Mitsubishi Power Lands Significant..." order) is a gas-turbine contract for Qatar's Facility E IWPP project (dated Jan 2026), not SOFC/SOEC, and out of scope.
Today's Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no item beyond the FuelCell Energy/StabilityMax story above.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 8, round 4, completing the cycle (Delta Electronics, Shell, Denso, Thermax), plus cycle 9 round 1 start (Reverion, Convion): no new items for any of the six; results repeated Ceres' 2024-vintage Delta/Shell/Denso/Thermax licensing background, the standing Doosan-Reverion $76.7-78M SOFC stack-supply story, and Convion's 2024 HD Korea Shipbuilding acquisition — all pre-dated.

Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). New: hosting a DOE/national-lab-backed R&D testbed (StabilityMax) in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
